## Body

## Security verdict: BLOCK

PR #229 at **63a2ba523c2a104ff418f3f1d7baaa37a47cda11**, round 1 under C33/C34. Reviewed the eight-file delta and relevant installer/launcher paths. PM confirmed the cross-account path-control finding blocks.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| S229-001 | 🟠 HIGH | `harness/scripts/install-pij-rs.sh` | 25-31 | Writable installation ancestors permit cross-account executable replacement or temp-path redirection | 9/10 |

### S229-001: directory-entry control is not protected by file chmod

The script has no restrictive umask. It runs `mkdir -p` for `$HOME/.local/share/pij/bin`, chooses predictable `.pij-rs.$$.tmp`, copies to it using ordinary `cp`, then chmods the file to 0755 and renames it. Existing ancestry/ownership is not checked; temporary creation is not exclusive.

**Required precondition:** another UID can traverse the preceding ancestors and write an installation ancestor, for example a shared-group home/path with inherited umask 0002 creating 0775 directories, or an already group/world-writable ancestor. Umask 0002 alone is insufficient if a private ancestor prevents traversal. The normal private-home/umask-022 setup described for macOS is not being reported as exposed by default; no deployed permissions were inspected.

Under that condition, the other UID can replace the installed executable or redirect its directory entry; the next PATH, bounce or login launch executes their code as the victim. The same directory control permits a planted predictable temporary path to redirect `cp`. Chmodding the temporary file does not prevent replacement of directory entries. This crosses C33's user-account boundary; it is not a malicious same-user environment claim.

Required cheap repair:

- Create new installation-directory components with mode 0700, using `mkdir -m`.
- Refuse an existing installation directory or ancestor under HOME that is group/world-writable or not owned by the user; do not silently chmod the whole home or unrelated paths.
- Use exclusive `mktemp` creation inside the verified target directory, then preserve atomic rename and executable file modes.

### Other checks and deployment qualification

Quoted installer operands preserve spaces/newlines as arguments. Same-directory rename replaces the directory entry without rewriting the running executable's inode, provided the hierarchy is trustworthy. Rust bounce passes separate arguments, but its absolute-file check does not validate ownership (`crates/cli/src/bounce/mod.rs:70-80,130-153,267-293`).

Install/bounce/LaunchAgent paths use the installed copy through the PATH link (`justfile:73-75,688-697,723-732`); the inherited shim uses a separate-argv process call, not interpolated shell text (`harness/scripts/pij-cli.cjs:79-107`). The doctor detects target-resolving and broken PATH entries, not unsafe permissions (`justfile:639-662`). Existing nested shell/XML handling was not independently proven for unusual path characters.

**S229-N001, deployment risk:** the new `~/.local/share/pij/bin/pij-rs` needs the documented Defender process exclusion added by the authorized admin/IT owner. Old exclusions do not automatically migrate; no exclusion or launch-cost deployment verification was performed.

**CI proof:** clean detached worktree HEAD and GitHub/remote heads agree; GitHub reports CLEAN and all five checks successful. Run [42932179293](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42932179293) checked merge `f1828b9ead340fa58f376cd0b0a71a855f3503fb`, whose parents are main `5f9727e984c2cb86cb09c34a5ecd758f479f01d0` and this exact head. Linux Rust reports **2,433 passed, 6 skipped**, including `install_copies_the_build_outside_target_and_replaces_it_by_rename` in successful artifact `13816761435`. Node 22 reports **2,290 passed, 6 skipped**. These tests do not establish cross-UID path safety or actual macOS signed-binary replacement.

Source and Linux CI only; macOS-only paths were inspected, not compiled or executed. No local build/test/install, real permission probes, user-config/credential reads or heavy command was run; no machine-build baton was requested.
